thread:
chris: seeing p99 east->west jump during the 09:00 batch ramp, started ~09:02 and lasted ~6m. apps reporting stalled KV cache hits and retries.

olga: I caught it on grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/cluster/network?panelId=7 p95->p99 widened fast at 09:02.

maya: noticed same in trace service — token delivery delays line up with ToR egress queuing.

ben: any packet-drop counters? could be microbursts from batched traffic.

olga: pulled counters on suspects (ToR-12 -> host spine links). quick snippet:
```
ifconfig bond0
RX packets: 483920 errors:0 dropped:232 overruns:0 frame:0
TX packets: 482300 errors:0 dropped:0 overruns:0 carrier:0
```
not massive CRC errors but drops spike.

chris: ran a short tcpdump on host during next ramp window to confirm. command I ran: `sudo timeout 60 tcpdump -i bond0 -w /tmp/batch_ramp.pcap 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-push) != 0'` captured bursts with retransmits.

olga: switch counters show tail drops on egress queues, ToR shows buffer occupancy spikes at the start of batching window. likely microburst + insufficient buffer sizing.

maya: are we using jumbo frames / MTU 9000 on these racks? mismatch would cause fragmenting under load.

ben: checked host MTU: `ip link show` returns mtu 9000 on hosts, but ToR config shows mtu 1500 on some older spine links (ugh).

chris: that would explain sudden drop at ramp when many peers open long-lived connections and send large transcripts. some p99 latency from reassembly and retransmits.

olga: short-term mitigation: stagger batch starts by staggering the job scheduler by 200-500ms per rack. can do a config tweak in the batcher service.

maya: also we can push an autoscaler rule to limit concurrent open connections during the peak window (cheap to try).

ben: long-term fix: standardize MTU across fabric to 9000 or enable jumbo on the spine. coordinate change window with netops.

chris: another option: enable ECN on fabric to reduce tail drops + tune CoDel if supported by ToR. but needs careful testing.

olga: for RDMA nodes: RoCEv2 needs PFC for lossless; didn't see PFC configured on the affected ToR ports. if we rely on RoCE for KV, that’s a problem.

maya: which clusters are affected? only eu-west-1 GPU pool or others?

chris: so far eu-west-1 and one pool in us-east-1 with older ToR images. not global.

ben: I'm going to create a short runbook and temp mitigation: 1) stagger batcher by 300ms, 2) throttle inflight batches to 85% of current, 3) onboard network ops for MTU change.

chris: can someone open an infra ticket and assign to netops and eng-infra ops? add link to packet capture and grafana dashboard.

olga: opened ticket INFRA-4122 and attached pcap + counters. assigned to @netops. ticket: https://issues.internal/redwood/INFRA-4122

maya: implemented stagger patch in canary — will push to 50% of racks in eu-west-1 now. watch p99.

sre-bot: deploy canary: batcher-stagger v1.2 -> 50% eu-west-1 scheduled (10:15 UTC).

chris: after canary, p99 dropped ~40% during the next ramp. still seeing small jitter but no wide tail. good sign.

ben: next steps: schedule MTU standardization with netops, run nightly validation script to assert MTU/ToR settings, evaluate enabling ECN, and audit RoCE/PFC on RDMA hosts.

maya: cost note: reducing batch concurrency will slightly increase per-token infra cost; we should model impact if this extended beyond a day.

chris: agreed — for now prioritize availability. will update post-mtg with netops. :slightly_smiling_face:

ben: thanks everyone — monitoring alert thresholds updated to detect similar microburst tail-rises earlier.

sre-bot: alert rule "ew-latency-jitter" updated by ben at 10:42 UTC.

chris: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions appear.
